data.name: Damodara
data.short_meaning: God who can be held in the hands
data.long_meaning: Damodara is a name of Lord Krishna, which means 'God who can be held in the hands'. It is said that Lord Krishna, who is an embodiment of God, can be held in one's heart and mind, just as one holds a physical object in one's hands.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the idea of God being present in one's heart and mind, and the ability to connect with the divine through devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Damodara' is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, particularly among the Vaishnavas, who are devotees of Lord Vishnu and his various incarnations, including Krishna. The name is often used in Hindu scriptures, art, and literature to refer to Lord Krishna.
data.spiritual_significance: According to Hindu scriptures, Lord Krishna is more than just a physical being; he is an eternal and transcendent reality. The Name 'Damodara' emphasizes the idea that one can connect with this eternal reality through devotion and love. It serves as a reminder that God is not an abstract concept but a personal being who can be experienced and held close to one's heart.

historical_references.reference: According to Vaishnava scriptures, Damodara is a name of Krishna, derived from the Sanskrit words daman meaning 'to restrain' and udara meaning 'abdomen'. This name refers to the time when Krishna was bound by his mother Yashoda with ropes around his waist as a playful prank, although there are also interpretations that it refers to Krishna's later binding by Kamsa or the demon Ahlaka.
historical_references.time_period: Approximately 5000 years ago, during the Mahabharata era in ancient India

historical_references.reference: Another reference from the Bhagavata Purana describes Damodara as an aspect of Krishna, who was buried up to his neck by his mother Yashoda as a playful punishment. This episode is often depicted in Hindu art and literature.
historical_references.time_period: Between 3200 BCE and 1300 CE, during the Vedic period and the early medieval period in ancient India

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Damodara' is a significant name in Hinduism, referring to Lord Krishna as the one who holds the world on his belly. In modern context, this name is widely used in various platforms. In religious organizations such as the Hare Krishna Movement and ISKCON, Lord Krishna is revered as Damodara. Temples dedicated to Lord Krishna, particularly in India, often have images and statues of Damodara. Additionally, with the increasing trend of digitalization and online platforms, Damodara is also represented in various digital forms such as mobile applications, websites, and social media channels.

name_in_real_life.story: Priya Damodara from Delhi, India embodies the meaning of Damodara - "God who can be held in the hands". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Damodara signifies the one who holds the divine 'Gopal' or 'Mother Yasoda's' affectionate ropes on his chest, symbolizing deep attachment and devotion towards the divine.
